title: Request Terms: Giving Up Live Protection Coverage
content:
Live coverage under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans that the customer gives up closes on the day they confirm it, and what comes back to them is worked out from what they have actually paid toward the plan and the part of the term they will not now use.

The premium returned is fixed only after the benefit consumed by every claim entered against the plan stands recorded against it.

Ending coverage they paid for is the customer's alone to do, so the cancellation is confirmed by the customer on the protection service request record.

## How the action is taken

The desk unlocks the tool `confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. One call closes the coverage as cancelled with today as its closing date, raises a cancellation on the protection desk's request record already marked as confirmed by the customer, and books the premium coming back as a movement out of what they have paid toward the plan, paid out on the channel they choose and pointed at the premium entry it gives back. Afterwards the coverage reads as cancelled, no further claim can be opened on it, and the money shows in the coverage history as premium returned.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `protection_plan_id` | the reference number of the coverage record being given up, as returned by the protection coverage lookup | an id |
| `refund_amount` | the premium coming back to the customer | a positive amount in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the last step only; 0.00 where nothing comes back |
| `refund_channel` | how the customer wants the money returned | one of exactly six values, below |

The six values `refund_channel` takes: `in_store` where they will collect it at a Belrose counter; `online_portal` where it goes back to the card or account the customer manages on the Belrose website; `phone_agent` where it is taken back over the telephone on a card read out to the desk; `mail_check` where a cheque is posted to the address on the profile; `autopay` where it is credited to the standing arrangement the premium is collected on; and `not_applicable` where no money moves to the customer at all, which is the value to pass when the amount coming back is zero.

## What comes back

A single confirmation line naming the coverage that was cancelled, the date it closed on, the reference number minted for the cancellation on the desk's request record, the reference number minted for the premium-returned entry, and the amount returned in USD. The line being returned at all is what indicates the cancellation took effect; afterwards the coverage record reads cancelled and the returned premium appears in its history.
